100	
101	### Status Monitoring System
102	
103	**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
104	- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
105	- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
106	- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
107	- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks
108	
109	Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.
110	
111	**Parallel Execution:**
112	- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
113	- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`
114	
115	### Component CRUD Operations
116	
117	Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
118	- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
119	- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
120	- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`
121	
122	State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`
123	
124	### Credentials Management
125	
126	No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
127	implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
128	writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
129	the credential manager *and* in plaintext:
130	
131	| Storage | Backend | Notes |
132	|---------|---------|-------|
133	| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
134	| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
135	| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |
136	
137	`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
138	The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
139	context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
140	pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
141	to the other one.
142	
143	The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
144	`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
145	second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
146	first one holds.
147	
148	`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
149	`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
150	is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
151	the auth view.
152	
153	## Testing
154	
155	Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
156	- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
157	- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests
158	
159	Use table-driven tests where appropriate.
160	
161	**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
162	only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
163	(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
164	run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.
165	
166	**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
167	`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
168	the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
169	it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
170	writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
171	`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
172	`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
173	(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
174	tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
175	`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
176	`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.
177	
178	**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
179	port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
180	the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
181	`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
182	runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
183	(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
184	D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).
185	
186	- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
187	  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
188	  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
189	  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
190	- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
191	  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
192	- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
193	  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
194	- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
195	  enforces it yet.
196	
197	**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
198	`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
199	literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
200	`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
201	panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
202	`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
203	colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
204	with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
205	hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
206	`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
207	(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
208	a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
209	and no key action fires (Rule 111).
210	
211	**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
212	`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
213	(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
214	handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
215	matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
216	`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
217	`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
218	`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.
219	
220	## Dependencies
221	
222	Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
223	- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
224	- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
225	- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
226	- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
227	- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
228	- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
229	- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client

104	  `docker` (`docker-hosted`, `docker-proxy`): two group members with the same label. Display
105	  only, keys are URL + prefix; flagged for the PM, not fixed here.

107	## Non-functional requirements
108	
109	- **No bench in `mise run test`/`ci`** (criterion 5): fixtures are embedded files; the fake
110	  server is `httptest` on loopback; nothing reads `NEXUS_BENCH_*` or the secrets file.
111	- **No leak** (criterion 1): every fixture passes a leak check in `mise run test`; the recorder
112	  runs the same check, plus an exact search for the real passwords, before writing anything.
113	- **No hand-written answer can pass as measured**: a fixture is either byte-identical to its
114	  dated evidence under `docs/measurements/` or carries `# recorded-by: nexus-bench record`.
115	- **Recorder safety**: credentials only to the loopback origins of the descriptor, Basic only,
116	  GET only, a closed list of path shapes (no manifest, no blob: a read through the proxy caches,
117	  F9), no redirect followed, bodies bounded at 1 MiB, nothing written on any error, atomic
118	  writes, no secret in argv, output or file.
119	- **Load**: about 30 small files (a few hundred bytes each); test runtime well under a second.
120	- **Exploitability**: one command regenerates (`mise run nexus-bench:record`), refuses on a
121	  drifted bench with the command to run (`nexus-bench:reset`), and writes nothing for an answer
122	  that did not change apart from its date.
123	
124	## Options
125	
126	### Where the fixtures live
127	
128	| Option | For | Against |
129	|---|---|---|
130	| A. Tests read `docs/measurements/nexus-catalog/` directly | one copy | regeneration would overwrite dated evidence of a measurement note; tests depend on a docs path; no `embed` (outside the module package tree) |
131	| **B. Copy into `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/<campaign>/`, embedded** (recommended) | dated evidence stays as measured; regeneration rewrites fixtures only; `go:embed` makes every test package find them whatever its directory; `go test` cache tracks them | two copies of NX-03; mitigated by the provenance test (byte-identical or `recorded-by`) |
132	| C. Move the files and repoint the note | one copy | rewrites a published measurement note; a regeneration then silently changes what the note cites |
133	
134	### Where the shared code lives
135	
136	| Option | For | Against |
137	|---|---|---|
138	| `internal/testutil/nexusfixture` | matches `internal/testutil/loopback` | the recorder (a non-test dev tool) would import a testutil package, against the convention "imported from `_test.go` only" |
139	| **`internal/nexusfixture` (format, parse, load, redact, leak check; no `testing`) + `internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus` (the `httptest` server; `testing.TB`)** (recommended) | the recorder imports only the first; `testing`/`httptest` stay out of the `nexus-bench` binary; `dk` imports neither | two packages |
140	
141	### How a fixture is regenerated
142	
143	| Option | For | Against |
144	|---|---|---|
145	| A shell/curl script | close to what NX-03 did | reads the secrets in a script, bypasses every guard of `nexusbench` (D-A: no bash) |
146	| **A `record` subcommand of `nexus-bench` + `mise run nexus-bench:record`** (recommended) | reuses descriptor, secrets store, loopback checks, dataset comparison and the guarded REST client; testable on fakes | needs a body-keeping client method in `nexusapi.go` |
147	
148	The request to replay is read **from the fixture itself** (method, target, `Host`, request
149	headers, identity from the file name): the fixture is its own spec. NX-04/NX-05 add
150	**request-only** files (`# record: pending`, no response section) and run `record` to fill
151	them: no code change for them, unless they need a new request shape (Bearer token step,
152	multi-exchange), for which the format already reserves the `###` separator.
153	
154	## Design
155	
156	### Fixture format (one file = one fixture; the NX-03 format, made explicit)
157	
158	```
159	# scenario: <free text>                      required
160	# nexus: <version> <EDITION> (<free text>)   required; version = first token, edition = second
161	# measured: <YYYY-MM-DD>[, <free text>]      required
162	# account: <free text>                       required (identity comes from the file name)
163	# redacted: <free text>                      required
164	# state: <nominal|upstream-cut|...>          optional, default nominal (NX-04)
165	# record: <replay|skip: reason|pending>      optional, default replay
166	# recorded-by: nexus-bench record            set by the recorder only
167	<blank>
168	<METHOD> <target> HTTP/1.1
169	Host: <host:port>
170	[Authorization: Basic <redacted> | Bearer <redacted>]
171	[Accept: ...]
172	<blank>
173	HTTP/1.1 <code> <reason>
174	<whitelisted headers>
175	<blank>
176	<body | <empty body> | <HTML body omitted: N bytes, <title>T</title>>>
177	[### then another exchange, same shape (NX-05: token step, redirect chain)]
178	```
179	
180	- File name `<scenario>--<admin|pull|anon>.http`; identity from the suffix only.
181	- Body: the text after the blank line, one trailing `\n` removed. A verbatim body with a
182	  `Content-Length` header must have that length (import integrity check).
183	- Stub bodies replay as: empty for `<empty body>`; a minimal
184	  `<html><head><title>T</title></head></html>` for the HTML stub (DevDesk never reads a non-200
185	  body; a test that needs the real body cannot use a stub, and the loader says which is which).
186	- `Format(Parse(b)) == b` for every NX-03 file (round trip), so the recorder writes the same
187	  format.
188

190	
191	`internal/nexusfixture` (no `testing` import):

193	```go

199	    State      string // "" = nominal
200	    Record     string // "" = replay, "pending", "skip: <reason>"
201	    RecordedBy string // "" for an imported NX-03 file

205	    Method, Target, Host string // Target = path + raw query as recorded
206	    RequestHeader        http.Header

233

241	`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus` (imported from `_test.go` files only):
242	
243	```go
244	const Password = "REDACTED"              // accepted for every account
245	func User(id nexusfixture.Identity) string       // admin -> "admin", pull -> "bench-pull", anon -> ""
246	type Server struct{ /* one httptest.Server per recorded Host */ }
247	func New(t testing.TB, fixtures ...nexusfixture.Fixture) *Server
248	func (s *Server) URL(recordedHost string) string // "127.0.0.1:30481" -> "http://127.0.0.1:NNNNN"
249	func (s *Server) Hits(fixtureName string) int

252	Matching, in order: recorded `Host` (one `httptest` server each), method, identity (no
253	`Authorization` = anon; `Basic` with `User(id)` and `Password` = that identity; anything else is
254	unmatched), then target: exact path + query; else the **catalog tolerance**: a request
255	`GET P?n=N` (no `last`) matches a fixture `GET P` recorded without query when its answer is 200,
256	has no `Link` and lists at most `N` names. Evidence: `page-group-n1000--admin` and
257	`catalog-group-connector-30482--admin` are identical (pinned by a test); for hosted and proxy it
258	is an inference (only `n=2` and no-`n` were measured), stated in the code comment and in
259	`nexus-bench.md`. Unmatched → `t.Errorf("no recorded answer for %s %s as %s")` and `501`: an
260	unrecorded answer is never invented. Replay: status, whitelisted headers except
261	`Content-Length` (recomputed), `Link`/`WWW-Authenticate`/`Location` with
262	`http://<recorded Host>` rewritten to the matching fake server's URL, body or stub.

268	func (c *client) exchange(ctx context.Context, method, target string, header http.Header) (status int, h http.Header, body []byte, err error)
269	
270	// record.go

272	    Origins    map[string]string // recorded Host -> base URL; loopback URLs of the descriptor only
273	    Descriptor Descriptor
274	    Secrets    Secrets

276	    Campaigns  []string          // default: all

280	}

285	### Data flow
286	
287	Test time: `fakenexus.New(t, nexusfixture.Load("catalog")...)` → `imagesearch.CatalogSearcher`
288	(real `oci.ListCatalogContext`) or `registrymgr.NexusDetector.DetectGroup` against
289	`s.URL("127.0.0.1:30481"|"127.0.0.1:30482")` → `Classify` / returned error → assertions.

292	REST probe → dataset comparison (`matches` required, else "run `mise run nexus-bench:reset`")
293	→ secrets → for each non-skipped fixture: request from the file → origin check → `exchange` →
294	`Redact` → version from `Server:` must equal the descriptor's → `CheckLeaks` with the real
295	passwords and their Basic forms → unchanged apart from `measured:`? keep the file : atomic
296	write with `measured:` today and `recorded-by`.

300	No data migration. NX-03 files are copied (not moved); the measurement note keeps its paths and
301	gets one added paragraph. Reversible by a revert; nothing irreversible (test-only packages and a

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

17	## Project Overview
18	
19	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
20	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
21	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
22	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
23	- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
24	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
25	- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
26	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
27	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
28	- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

30	## Build and Development Commands
31	
32	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
33	
34	```bash
35	# Development (fastest)
36	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
37	go run .
38	
39	# Build
40	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
41	mise run run          # Build and run
42	
43	# Testing
44	mise run test         # Run all tests
45	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
46	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
47	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
48	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
49	
50	# Code Quality
51	mise run fmt          # Format code
52	mise run vet          # Run go vet
53	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
54	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
55	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
56	mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR
57	
58	# Installation
59	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
60	```
61	
62	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

64	## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules
65	
66	- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
67	- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
68	- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
69	- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
70	- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
71	- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.
72	
73	## Releases
74	
75	Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

77	## Architecture

80	**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
81	the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are

100	
101	### Status Monitoring System
102	
103	**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
104	- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
105	- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
106	- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
107	- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks
108	
109	Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.
110	
111	**Parallel Execution:**
112	- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
113	- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`
114	
115	### Component CRUD Operations
116	
117	Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
118	- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
119	- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
120	- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`
121	
122	State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`
123	
124	### Credentials Management
125	
126	No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
127	implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
128	writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
129	the credential manager *and* in plaintext:
130	
131	| Storage | Backend | Notes |
132	|---------|---------|-------|
133	| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
134	| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
135	| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |
136	
137	`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
138	The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
139	context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
140	pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
141	to the other one.
142	
143	The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
144	`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
145	second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
146	first one holds.
147	
148	`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
149	`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
150	is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
151	the auth view.
152	
153	## Testing
154	
155	Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
156	- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
157	- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests
158	
159	Use table-driven tests where appropriate.
160	
161	**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
162	only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
163	(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
164	run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.
165	
166	**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
167	`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
168	the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
169	it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
170	writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
171	`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
172	`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
173	(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
174	tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
175	`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
176	`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.
177	
178	**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
179	port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
180	the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
181	`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
182	runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
183	(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
184	D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).
185	
186	- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
187	  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
188	  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
189	  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
190	- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
191	  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
192	- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
193	  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
194	- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
195	  enforces it yet.
196	
197	**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
198	`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
199	literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
200	`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
201	panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
202	`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
203	colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
204	with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
205	hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
206	`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
207	(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
208	a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
209	and no key action fires (Rule 111).
210	
211	**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
212	`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
213	(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
214	handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
215	matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
216	`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
217	`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
218	`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

220	## Dependencies
221	
222	Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):

237	## Code Conventions
238	
239	- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
240	- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
241	- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
242	- Bubbletea models define their own message types
243	- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
244	- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
245	- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
246	- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
247	- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)
248	
249	## Critical Bubble Tea Rules
250	
251	**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
252	- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
253	- `View()` is read-only
254	- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages
255	
256	**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
257	- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
258	- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`
259	
260	**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
261	`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
262	router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
263	`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.
264	
265	**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

107	## Non-functional requirements
108	
109	- **No bench in `mise run test`/`ci`** (criterion 5): fixtures are embedded files; the fake
110	  server is `httptest` on loopback; nothing reads `NEXUS_BENCH_*` or the secrets file.
111	- **No leak** (criterion 1): every fixture passes a leak check in `mise run test`; the recorder
112	  runs the same check, plus an exact search for the real passwords, before writing anything.
113	- **No hand-written answer can pass as measured**: a fixture is either byte-identical to its
114	  dated evidence under `docs/measurements/` or carries `# recorded-by: nexus-bench record`.
115	- **Recorder safety**: credentials only to the loopback origins of the descriptor, Basic only,
116	  GET only, a closed list of path shapes (no manifest, no blob: a read through the proxy caches,
117	  F9), no redirect followed, bodies bounded at 1 MiB, nothing written on any error, atomic
118	  writes, no secret in argv, output or file.
119	- **Load**: about 30 small files (a few hundred bytes each); test runtime well under a second.
120	- **Exploitability**: one command regenerates (`mise run nexus-bench:record`), refuses on a
121	  drifted bench with the command to run (`nexus-bench:reset`), and writes nothing for an answer
122	  that did not change apart from its date.

154	## Design
155	
156	### Fixture format (one file = one fixture; the NX-03 format, made explicit)
157	
158	```
159	# scenario: <free text>                      required
160	# nexus: <version> <EDITION> (<free text>)   required; version = first token, edition = second
161	# measured: <YYYY-MM-DD>[, <free text>]      required
162	# account: <free text>                       required (identity comes from the file name)
163	# redacted: <free text>                      required
164	# state: <nominal|upstream-cut|...>          optional, default nominal (NX-04)
165	# record: <replay|skip: reason|pending>      optional, default replay
166	# recorded-by: nexus-bench record            set by the recorder only
167	<blank>
168	<METHOD> <target> HTTP/1.1
169	Host: <host:port>
170	[Authorization: Basic <redacted> | Bearer <redacted>]
171	[Accept: ...]
172	<blank>
173	HTTP/1.1 <code> <reason>
174	<whitelisted headers>
175	<blank>
176	<body | <empty body> | <HTML body omitted: N bytes, <title>T</title>>>
177	[### then another exchange, same shape (NX-05: token step, redirect chain)]
178	```
179	
180	- File name `<scenario>--<admin|pull|anon>.http`; identity from the suffix only.
181	- Body: the text after the blank line, one trailing `\n` removed. A verbatim body with a
182	  `Content-Length` header must have that length (import integrity check).
183	- Stub bodies replay as: empty for `<empty body>`; a minimal
184	  `<html><head><title>T</title></head></html>` for the HTML stub (DevDesk never reads a non-200
185	  body; a test that needs the real body cannot use a stub, and the loader says which is which).
186	- `Format(Parse(b)) == b` for every NX-03 file (round trip), so the recorder writes the same
187	  format.

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

101:**D161 — DEVDESK-510 (NX-07): a refused members endpoint is a typed error, not an empty group. Decided (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-510-plan.md`, implemented on branch `feat/devdesk-510-nexus-members-refused`, archived 2026-11-18; the wording validated by the user, and the transient `unreachable` state decided by the user on 2026-11-18): (1) `registrymgr.MembersRefusedError` (`Group`, `Status`, `Anonymous`, `Cause` → `*oci.StatusError`, `Is` `ErrMembersRefused`, `Unwrap` to the status error) is returned for a 401 or 403 from the management API on `GET /v1/repositories/{format}/group/{name}` only; the anonymous retry decides when the first attempt was refused. Network failure, deadline, 404, 5xx, off-origin redirect and unreadable reply are propagated and not cached (D23); an empty member list is a settled empty group, not an error. Its text carries the group and the status, never a URL, header or body. Rejected: a bare sentinel (it cannot say whether the request was anonymous), a result struct (interface churn). (2) The group cache file `registry-groups.json` moves to the envelope `{"version":2,"groups","refusals"}`. A refusal sits beside the listing, never inside it, and never touches the members known (D23); a successful listing, even empty, clears it. A legacy bare-map file keeps only the entries with a member, the empty ones are set aside (CA6), so they read as `never`; a version 2 or newer file is read as it is (a downgrade is accepted). One decoder, shared with the read-only MCP reader; writes are atomic, `0600`. (3) UI: the Members cell reads `denied` (`denied · N known · age` when a list survives), the status line is derived on every render (Warn for a refusal, Info for a settled empty group), and a transient failure reads `unreachable` in the footer at level Error with nothing cached. The Members column stays `SizingContent` with `MinWidth` 16, so the visibility threshold does not move. Members declared by hand are listed at group level. (4) MCP `registries_list` gains `members_refused` (`at`, `age_seconds`, `status`, `anonymous`), never an error text. (5) The follow-ups of D160 are done here: the `format` segment is escaped with `url.PathEscape`, and the logs use `%q` for the server's `type` and `format`. Out of scope, recorded: `refusedStatus` in `internal/imagesearch/verdict.go` (a management-API status is not yet told apart from a registry refusal; no Nexus path reaches it today); `repoName` is not escaped in the endpoints; the names of members returned by the server are not validated, and ANSI sequences in the table cells are pre-existing; concurrent writes of the group cache are last-writer-wins (pre-existing lost-update race, a candidate follow-up with one cache instance or a file lock); the hypothesis that the detail endpoint answers 403 to a pull-only account is to confirm on the NX-03 bench; nit: the status line reads `1 declared by hand are used`. No ADR: local, derived data, reversible by a revert (a revert reads the v2 file as empty groups, `never`). **Plane:** DEVDESK-510 (NX-07); NX-09 (DEVDESK, depends on NX-07) can now read `unknown` from the refusal. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-510-plan.md`, `internal/registrymgr/refusal.go`, `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go`, `internal/cache/registry_groups.go`, `internal/ui/oci_resources/members_refused.go`, `internal/mcp/registry_tools.go`; D23, D160.**
103:**D160 — DEVDESK-509 (NX-06): the Nexus REST client handles errors like the `internal/oci` registry client. Decided (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-509-plan.md`, 2026-11-17): (1) The client reuses `internal/oci`: a third source, `oci.SourceManagementAPI`, in `oci.StatusError` (`management API returned <code>`), for a registry manager's own REST API. No copy, no new package, no import cycle (`internal/oci` depends on no other `devdesk` package). Rejected: a `registrymgr.StatusError` (a second type for one concept) and an extracted `internal/httpguard` (out of proportion here). (2) A non-200 answer is a `*oci.StatusError` with no status line, body or header echoed, so no secret reaches the error. A context error is never a `StatusError`: a failed body read returns `read Nexus response: <ctx error>` (wrapped with `%w`) when the context is done, so `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled | context.DeadlineExceeded)` holds whatever `net/http` returns. (3) The 1 MiB reply cap (`maxNexusResponse`) stays in `nexus.go`, not shared with the token cap (`maxTokenResponse`), which bounds another reply. (4) Behaviour change: a 200 reply that is empty, or valid JSON with no `type` (`{}`, `null`), is a failed discovery (`errEmptyReply`, `errNoRepositoryType`, wrapped with the endpoint), not cached as "not a group" (D23); the members last known are kept. Hypothesis, to confirm in review: Nexus always sends `type` on `GET /service/rest/v1/repositories/{name}`. Syntax errors were already rejected. (5) Criteria 1 and 2 (same-origin redirect and 1 MiB cap) shipped with DEVDESK-412 (D156); this entry adds only tests: another scheme, and 302 and 307 for the off-origin refusal. No ADR: local and reversible by a revert. Follow-ups, out of scope: NX-07 (`fetchRepoMeta` and `fetchGroupMembers` swallow the step-2 errors, so a failure erases the members known); `internal/imagesearch/verdict.go` (`refusedStatus`) should test `Source == oci.SourceRegistry` rather than `!= SourceToken`, so a management-API `StatusError` is not read as a refusal (no Nexus path reaches it today); `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go` logs `result.Type` and `result.Format` with `%s`, so a hostile server can inject ANSI sequences or newlines into the logs: use `%q`. **Plane:** DEVDESK-509 (NX-06). Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-509-plan.md`, `internal/oci/registry.go`, `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go`, `internal/registrymgr/nexus_errors_test.go`; D142, D156.**

## 2026-11-17 — DEVDESK-506 (NX-03): `_catalog` measured on the bench (no decision)

Source: `docs/measurements/2026-11-17-nexus-catalog.md` (raw responses in `docs/measurements/nexus-catalog/`). Nexus `3.98.1-01` Community, bench `datomir`. Facts are measured; nothing is decided.

1. **H1 contradicted.** `_catalog` does not prefix names with the member repository (`api`, not `docker-hosted/api`). There is no global `/v2/_catalog` on the HTTP port (404); only the group connector on its own port (30482) answers at the root.
2. **H2 confirmed for the bench account.** The `bench-pull` and anonymous accounts get the same full lists as admin. The filtering case stays untested: no account in the bench is restricted to one repository.
3. **Correction of 2026-08-10 (`docs/backlog.md` §3.18).** The detailed repository endpoint refuses the pull account with 404 "Repository not found" on this version, not 403. Anonymous gets 403. The version of the earlier instance is unknown.
4. **IS-07 contradicted for members addressed by host and path.** Each member answers on its own path catalogue, so one walk per member is needed. On the group connector one walk finds all six names, but names carry no member, and `shared/base` resolves to the first member only.
5. **Side effect on the bench.** A HEAD on a manifest through `docker-proxy` cached `shared/base:1.0` there. `nexus-bench:status` reports `dataset: differs (1 image)`. Reset it before NX-04.

Sections to revisit (none decided):
- **IS-03** criteria 2 and 5 (`repo_prefix`, parade R1): the prefix filter keeps nothing on this version.
- **IS-07** criterion 2, `walks.go` and D140 (shared-walk key): one walk per member, not per host; the group needs no per-member split.
- **NX-10**: its start condition (NX-03 contradicts H1 or H2) is met by H1. Whether to rebuild the prefix (`/v2/<prefix>/_catalog`) or use REST search is for the user to decide before NX-10 is promoted.
- **NX-04**: start from a known state (see point 5).
- **NX-05**: group pagination with `n=2` returns duplicates on the group connector; not yet explained.

No ADR. Decision on H1 is the user's.

1. **Decided: work the jobs registry tracks shows the shared activity dot (`●`/`○`) in the footer, not a braille frame.** The view passes the router's blink phase with `SetBlinkPhase`. Scope: the 8 `jobs.FrameMsg` consumers, plus the explorer's load lines (option B). Details and rejected options are in D127 (`docs/backlog.md` §1.1).
2. **Decided: the router sends only the blink.** `jobs.FrameMsg` drops its braille frame and the 100 ms cadence goes, so 2 ticks per second run while jobs run, instead of 10. Source: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-341-plan.md` (branch `feat/DEVDESK-341-footer-activity-dot`, untracked).

101	**D161 — DEVDESK-510 (NX-07): a refused members endpoint is a typed error, not an empty group. Decided (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-510-plan.md`, implemented on branch `feat/devdesk-510-nexus-members-refused`, archived 2026-11-18; the wording validated by the user, and the transient `unreachable` state decided by the user on 2026-11-18): (1) `registrymgr.MembersRefusedError` (`Group`, `Status`, `Anonymous`, `Cause` → `*oci.StatusError`, `Is` `ErrMembersRefused`, `Unwrap` to the status error) is returned for a 401 or 403 from the management API on `GET /v1/repositories/{format}/group/{name}` only; the anonymous retry decides when the first attempt was refused. Network failure, deadline, 404, 5xx, off-origin redirect and unreadable reply are propagated and not cached (D23); an empty member list is a settled empty group, not an error. Its text carries the group and the status, never a URL, header or body. Rejected: a bare sentinel (it cannot say whether the request was anonymous), a result struct (interface churn). (2) The group cache file `registry-groups.json` moves to the envelope `{"version":2,"groups","refusals"}`. A refusal sits beside the listing, never inside it, and never touches the members known (D23); a successful listing, even empty, clears it. A legacy bare-map file keeps only the entries with a member, the empty ones are set aside (CA6), so they read as `never`; a version 2 or newer file is read as it is (a downgrade is accepted). One decoder, shared with the read-only MCP reader; writes are atomic, `0600`. (3) UI: the Members cell reads `denied` (`denied · N known · age` when a list survives), the status line is derived on every render (Warn for a refusal, Info for a settled empty group), and a transient failure reads `unreachable` in the footer at level Error with nothing cached. The Members column stays `SizingContent` with `MinWidth` 16, so the visibility threshold does not move. Members declared by hand are listed at group level. (4) MCP `registries_list` gains `members_refused` (`at`, `age_seconds`, `status`, `anonymous`), never an error text. (5) The follow-ups of D160 are done here: the `format` segment is escaped with `url.PathEscape`, and the logs use `%q` for the server's `type` and `format`. Out of scope, recorded: `refusedStatus` in `internal/imagesearch/verdict.go` (a management-API status is not yet told apart from a registry refusal; no Nexus path reaches it today); `repoName` is not escaped in the endpoints; the names of members returned by the server are not validated, and ANSI sequences in the table cells are pre-existing; concurrent writes of the group cache are last-writer-wins (pre-existing lost-update race, a candidate follow-up with one cache instance or a file lock); the hypothesis that the detail endpoint answers 403 to a pull-only account is to confirm on the NX-03 bench; nit: the status line reads `1 declared by hand are used`. No ADR: local, derived data, reversible by a revert (a revert reads the v2 file as empty groups, `never`). **Plane:** DEVDESK-510 (NX-07); NX-09 (DEVDESK, depends on NX-07) can now read `unknown` from the refusal. Sources: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-510-plan.md`, `internal/registrymgr/refusal.go`, `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go`, `internal/cache/registry_groups.go`, `internal/ui/oci_resources/members_refused.go`, `internal/mcp/registry_tools.go`; D23, D160.**

**D162 — DEVDESK-511 (NX-08a): recorded Nexus answers serve as regression tests, partial scope. Decided (plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-511-plan.md`, implemented on branch `feat/nexus-recorded-fixtures-devdesk-511`, 2026-11-18; the scope and the open questions settled by the user on 2026-11-18): (1) The measured answers of NX-03 (DEVDESK-506, `docs/measurements/nexus-catalog/`) are copied, already redacted, to `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/<campaign>/*.http` and embedded. The evidence stays as measured; a regeneration rewrites only the fixtures. Rejected: tests reading `docs/` (a regeneration would overwrite the evidence, and `go:embed` cannot reach outside the package), moving the files (rewrites a published note), a curl script (reads the secrets outside every guard of `nexusbench`), `internal/testutil` (the recorder would import a test-only package). (2) Format: one file is one fixture; the identity comes from the file name (`admin`, `pull`, `anon`). Provenance rule: a fixture without `recorded-by` is byte-identical to its evidence file, and `recorded-by: nexus-bench record` marks a regenerated one, so no hand-written answer passes as measured. (3) Fake Nexus: `internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus` (`httptest`, imported by `_test.go` only) replays the fixtures by recorded host, method, identity and path. An unmatched request fails the test and answers 501: an unrecorded answer is never invented. Catalog tolerance: `GET P?n=N` matches a recording of `GET P` made without `n` when it is a 200 with no `Link` and at most `N` names. Measured on the group connector only (`page-group-n1000--admin` equals `catalog-group-connector-30482--admin`); inferred for hosted and proxy repositories (only `n=2` and no `n` were measured), and stated as such in the code and in `nexus-bench.md`. (4) Recorder: `nexus-bench record` and `mise run nexus-bench:record` (no kubectl) regenerate the fixtures from the bench. Guards: loopback origins of the descriptor only, GET and Basic only, a closed path list (no manifest, no blob, nothing through the proxy caches), no redirect followed, bodies capped at 1 MiB, the `Server:` version and edition checked against the descriptor, a leak check with the real passwords before any write, all-or-nothing writes, and an unchanged answer keeps its file (only `measured:` may differ). (5) Stale signal: `TestFixturesMatchTheBenchVersion` (`internal/nexusfixture/stale_test.go`) compares each fixture's version and edition with `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` and fails `mise run test` with the command to run (`mise run nexus-bench:record`). Reference: `descriptor.json`, not `testdata/descriptor.example.json`, which is the golden of `Defaults()` and does not move when the bench does. The failure is wanted: a bumped bench forces the regeneration into the same PR. (6) Partial scope: criterion 2 (verdicts) and criterion 6 (regeneration) are covered for the single-request GET fixtures of NX-03 only. Not covered: `failed` (no failing answer was measured in NX-03; the 502 of a cut upstream belongs to NX-04), `Cached only` (decided by the UI from the config, meaningless before H3 is measured), the Bearer realm, redirects, pagination over several pages and port or path routing beyond the two bench origins (NX-05). Their recordings go to **NX-08b, DEVDESK-580**, which depends on NX-04 and NX-05: request-only files (`record: pending`), the `state:` key and multi-exchange files (`###`), with no code change expected. (7) Decisions taken with the user on 2026-11-18: (a) **the 404 of the pull account on the detailed group endpoint is frozen as the current behaviour.** On 3.98.1-01 `bench-pull` gets 404 `Repository not found` where D161 expected 403; the fixture test `TestDetectGroupOnMeasuredNexusAnswers` (`internal/registrymgr/nexus_fixture_test.go`) pins that the discovery fails (`unreachable`, footer Error, nothing cached), not `denied`. `TestNexusMembersOtherStatusIsNotARefusal` is unchanged. Changing it is **DEVDESK-578 (NX-07b)**: a 404 on a group's detailed endpoint, after the generic endpoint said `group`, is a members refusal. Rejected here: changing `membersFailure` or `refusedStatus` in a fixture task (UI wording, cache and MCP consequences). (b) **The interface tests contradicted by H1 and IS-07 are annotated, not changed.** `internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_catalog_share_test.go` (`TestThreeNexusMembersOnOneCatalogWalkItOnce` and its siblings) serve one prefixed `/v2/_catalog` for three members on one host; 3.98.1 does not (no prefix, no shared host catalog). Assertions unchanged; the comments name **DEVDESK-579**, where the approach is the user's decision (member's own path, REST search, or other). (c) **The root `GET /v2/_catalog?n=1000` 404 has no measured answer** (the NX-03 root was recorded without `n`). Deferred to **DEVDESK-580**; the skip test in `internal/imagesearch/catalog_fixture_test.go` activates itself when the fixture exists. (d) The `n=1000` tolerance above is measured on the group only, as stated in (3). (8) Known limits accepted, not fixed here: (a) the library does not check the anonymous side of the data set: a bench with anonymous access cut cannot record its anonymous fixtures correctly; (b) the skip fixtures and the multi-exchange fixtures are not exempted from the stale check; to decide before NX-05; (c) `CheckLeaks` does not detect exotic encodings of a secret, beyond the plain and Base64 forms of the bench passwords; (d) a local process listening on the bench port receives the Basic header before the `Server:` version check (loopback only, but the check comes after the send); (e) `storedSecrets` (`internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench/record.go`) duplicates `adminFromStore` (`internal/nexusbench/components.go`): two readers of the same secrets store, to merge. No ADR: local test tooling and a dev-tool subcommand, reversible by a revert; `dk` imports none of it. **Plane:** DEVDESK-511 (NX-08a) carries this partial scope; DEVDESK-577 (NX-08.10) is the task; DEVDESK-578 (NX-07b), DEVDESK-579 and DEVDESK-580 (NX-08b) are the follow-ups. Reference: `descriptor.json`, not `testdata/descriptor.example.json`, which is the golden of `Defaults()` and does not move when the bench does. The failure is wanted: a bumped bench forces the regeneration into the same PR. Rejected here: changing `membersFailure` or `refusedStatus` in a fixture task (UI wording, cache and MCP consequences). # CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
